title: Keep only the unbeaten options

blocks.text: A school district compares options for its bus routes. Each option is scored on several measures; some are better high (students served, on-time rate) and some better low (cost, longest ride). Before anyone argues about weights, the district wants the list cut down to the options worth arguing about: those that no other option beats.

Write `unbeaten(options, senses)` in `pareto.py`. `options` maps each option's name to its tuple of measures, and `senses[m]` is `"max"` or `"min"` for measure `m`. Return the names of the options that no other option dominates, in the sense of the lesson: at least as good in every measure and strictly better in at least one. The helper `dominates(p, q, senses)` is there for you to fill in and use.

Before coding, decide what your function should do with two options whose measures are all equal, and with an option that ties another on one measure and loses on the other; then check your decision against the definition.

cases.says: an option some other option beats on every measure is dropped
two identical options do not knock each other out
an option that ties on one measure and loses on the other is dropped
for a measure marked min, the lower value is the better one
